issue.title: `inplace_vector` insertion functions do not specify iterator invalidation

discussion.p:
does not specify iterator and reference invalidation for insertion functions.
According to p67, the current wording of implies that `inplace_vector` insertions do not invalidate iterators and references or change the values of objects in the container:

blockquote.p: Unless otherwise specified (either explicitly or by defining a function in terms of other functions), invoking a container member function or passing a container as an argument to a library function shall not invalidate iterators to, or change the values of, objects within that container.

discussion.p: specified reference invalidation for `insert` and `emplace`, for example:

blockquote.pre: constexpr iterator insert(const_iterator position, value_type&& x);

blockquote.p: Effects: Inserts `x` at position and invalidates all references to elements after position.

discussion.p:
This wording was removed in with no corresponding changelog entry.
On the other hand, p19 still specifies invalidation for erasure:

blockquote.p: Effects: Invalidates iterators and references at or after the point of the erase.

discussion.p: For comparison, /2 specifies invalidation for insertion without reallocation:

blockquote.p: If no reallocation happens, then references, pointers, and iterators before the insertion point remain valid but those at or after the insertion point, including the past-the-end iterator, are invalidated.

discussion.p: I took a quick look at libstdc++ implementation. I believe an insertion to `inplace_vector` can shift elements, therefore it is inconsistent with p67.

blockquote.p:
-1- Let `n` be the value of `size()` before this call for the `append_range` overload, and `distance(begin, position)` otherwise.
-2- Complexity: Linear in the number of elements inserted plus the distance to the end of the vector.
-3- Remarks: References, pointers, and iterators before the insertion point remain valid, but those at or after the insertion point, including the past-the-end iterator, are invalidated. If an exception is thrown other than by the copy constructor, move constructor, assignment operator, or move assignment operator of `T` or by any `InputIterator` operation, there are no effects. Otherwise, if an exception is thrown, then size() ≥ n and elements in the range `begin() + [0, n)` are not modified.

-4- Returns: `back()`.
-5- Throws: `bad_alloc` or any exception thrown by the initialization of the inserted element.
-6- Complexity: Constant.
-7- Remarks: If an element is appended, invalidates the past-the-end iterator. If an exception is thrown, there are no effects on `*this`.

-8- Let `vals` denote a pack: […]
-9- Preconditions: […]
-10- Effects: If size() < capacity() is `true`, appends an object of type `T` direct-non-list-initialized with `vals...`. Otherwise, there are no effects.
-11- Returns: `nullopt` if `size() == capacity()` is `true`, otherwise optional<reference>(in_place, back()).
-12- Throws: Nothing unless an exception is thrown by the initialization of the inserted element.
-13- Complexity: Constant.
-14- Remarks: If an element is appended, invalidates the past-the-end iterator. If an exception is thrown, there are no effects on `*this`.
